The Principal Surgical Technician (PST) is an advanced allied health professional and integral member of the perioperative team, providing expert technical support to ensure safe, efficient, and high-quality patient care across a variety of surgical specialties. Working under the direction of the surgeon and the general supervision of the registered nurse, the PST helps ensure that operative procedures are conducted under conditions that maximize patient safety and optimize surgical outcomes.
60% - Principal Surgical Technician Duties

The PST possesses advanced expertise in the theory and application of sterile and aseptic technique and combines extensive knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, surgical procedures, instrumentation, implants, and emerging surgical technologies to facilitate the successful performance of invasive therapeutic and diagnostic procedures. This role requires exceptional technical proficiency, professionalism, and the ability to anticipate the needs of the surgical team.

As a Subject Matter Expert (SME) within an assigned surgical specialty, the PST serves as the primary technical resource for instrumentation, equipment, implants, and supplies. The PST maintains comprehensive knowledge of specialty-specific procedures, surgical workflows, and technological advancements, ensuring the appropriate resources are available and functioning to support complex surgical interventions.

In addition to providing expert support, the PST functions as a leader, mentor, and preceptor within the perioperative environment. The incumbent serves as a content expert across specialties and disciplines within their area of expertise, providing guidance, training, and competency development for Surgical Technicians, Surgical Technician trainees, Registered Nurses, and other members of the interdisciplinary surgical team. The PST actively contributes to the development and standardization of surgical practices, instrumentation, and specialty workflows while promoting evidence-based practice and continuous quality improvement.

As an advanced practitioner, the Principal Surgical Technician is expected to exercise a high degree of autonomy, initiative, and sound judgment in applying established perioperative principles to complex or unusual clinical situations. Independent decision-making is expected within the scope of practice, with consultation from the Registered Nurse or Perioperative leadership available when appropriate. The PST demonstrates leadership through collaboration, problem-solving, operational expertise, and a commitment to excellence in patient care, supporting the mission and strategic goals of Perioperative Services.
Graduation or proof of completion of an accredited school of surgical technology or proof of completion of a US military surgical technology program
Commitment to excellence in patient care.
Adapts to change in a positive, professional and productive manner.
Ability to utilize medical terminology appropriately.
Knowledge of current trends in surgical technology.
Ability to cope during stressful situations and working in a highly paced environment including dealing with surgical emergencies.
Knowledge and understanding of principles of and practices of asepsis/sterile techniques.
Knowledge of instrumentation, supplies, and equipment usage and processing.
Working knowledge and understanding of common major surgical procedures for major surgical services.
Ability and dexterity to effectively work with micro sutures and micro instrumentation.
Ability to read, write, speak, and understand the English language.
Effective interpersonal skills.
Demonstrates accountability and professionalism at all times serving as a role model.
Sound assessment and decision making skills to respond quickly to changing patient care and staff needs.
